1	"""Deterministic 2D grid A* planner.
2	
3	Public entry points: ``plan(width, height, blocked, start, goal, costs=None,
4	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
5	max_cost=None)``, ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals,
6	costs=None, trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None,
7	snapshot=False, max_cost=None)``,
8	``replay(width, height, blocked, start, goal, path, costs=None,
9	dynamic_blocked=None, diagnose=False)`` and
10	``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)``.
11	
12	Semantics:
13	- Four-neighborhood moves, Manhattan heuristic. Without ``costs`` each step
14	  has unit cost. With ``costs`` (a height-by-width matrix of positive
15	  integers, row-major: ``costs[y][x]``) entering a cell costs that cell's
16	  value; the start cell's cost is never counted, so ``cost`` is the sum of
17	  the costs of the cells entered along the path.
18	- Tie-breaking is fully specified and order-independent: compare f, then h,
19	  then the (x, y) coordinate in lexicographic order.
20	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the nodes popped from the priority queue and
21	  closed for the first time (the goal counts when reached; stale heap
22	  entries and duplicate closings do not).
23	- Returns ``{"path": [...], "cost": int, "expanded": int}`` on success and
24	  ``{"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": int}`` when unreachable.
25	- When ``trace`` is true, both kinds of results additionally include
26	  ``expanded_nodes``: the list of coordinate tuples closed for the first
27	  time, in expansion order (includes the start, and the goal on success);
28	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. The field is omitted entirely when
29	  ``trace`` is false or omitted.
30	
31	Search budget (``max_expanded``):
32	- ``max_expanded`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key,
33	  value, exception type and validation order of the default behavior
34	  untouched. Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a
35	  bool: other types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise
36	  ``ValueError``. These checks run after all existing grid, costs,
37	  ``trace`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` validation (including the frame-0
38	  check) and before the search starts.
39	- The budget counts closed nodes (exactly what ``expanded`` counts); once
40	  the limit is reached no further node is closed. When the budget is
41	  provided the result always carries an additional ``status`` field:
42	  ``"found"`` when the goal was closed within the limit (the usual
43	  ``path``/``cost`` are returned), ``"unreachable"`` when the candidates
44	  were exhausted without reaching the goal, and ``"budget_exhausted"``
45	  when live candidates remained but the budget stopped the search (then
46	  ``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded`` is the actual closed
47	  count, at most ``max_expanded``).
48	- The budget applies identically in static and dynamic mode and never
49	  changes expansion order, path choice, trace entries or determinism: a
50	  budgeted trace is a prefix of the unbudgeted one. With ``trace=True``
51	  only actually closed nodes are recorded, so a zero budget records
52	  nothing -- even when ``start == goal`` a zero budget returns
53	  ``budget_exhausted`` with ``expanded == 0``; the single-point success
54	  result requires at least one closed node (``max_expanded >= 1``).
55	- ``replay`` is unaffected: it keeps validating candidate paths only and
56	  accepts no budget parameter.
57	
58	Cost limit (``max_cost``):
59	- ``max_cost`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key, value,
60	  exception type and validation order of the previous behavior untouched.
61	  Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a bool: other
62	  types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise ``ValueError``. The
63	  check runs after all existing grid, costs, ``trace``, ``dynamic_blocked``,
64	  ``max_expanded`` and ``snapshot`` validation and before the search
65	  starts.
66	- The limit caps the accumulated entering-cell cost of a route, measured
67	  from the start (the start cell still costs 0 and each entered cell costs
68	  its ``costs`` value, or 1 without ``costs``). A candidate whose
69	  accumulated cost would exceed the limit is discarded; a candidate at
70	  exactly the limit still competes. The limit applies identically in
71	  static mode, dynamic mode and ``plan_any``, and never changes expansion
72	  order, tie-breaks, the minimum-cost choice, the multi-goal endpoint
73	  comparison or trace entries.
74	- When ``max_cost`` is provided the result always carries ``status``:
75	  ``"found"`` on success, and on failure ``"cost_exhausted"`` when at
76	  least one candidate was discarded for exceeding the limit, otherwise
77	  ``"unreachable"`` (``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded``
78	  counts the actually closed nodes). When ``max_expanded`` is also given,
79	  a budget stop still takes priority with ``"budget_exhausted"``.
80	  ``trace`` keeps recording only actually closed nodes, and the
81	  ``start == goal`` single-point zero-cost result and the zero-budget
82	  rules are unchanged.
83	- With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint records the ``max_cost`` value
84	  when one was provided (and no new field when it was not). ``resume``
85	  treats a checkpoint without the field as ``None``, validates a present
86	  field with the same rules (``TypeError`` for wrong types, ``ValueError``
87	  for negative values or a state inconsistent with the limit) before any
88	  searching, and a resumed search is equivalent to one uninterrupted call
89	  with the same limit. ``replay`` accepts no ``max_cost`` parameter.
90	
91	Dynamic obstacles (``dynamic_blocked``):
92	- ``dynamic_blocked`` may be omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence, which
93	  leaves the static behavior above untouched. Otherwise it must be a
94	  sequence of frames; each frame is an iterable of grid coordinates that
95	  are blocked at that time frame. Frame 0 constrains ``start``; the
96	  coordinate at path index ``t`` must avoid both the static obstacles and
97	  frame ``t``, and frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame.
98	- Moves are still four-neighborhood only: no waiting in place and no
99	  repeated coordinates along the path. Because feasibility of a route
100	  depends on the coordinates it already visited, candidates that reach the
101	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
102	  states and are never merged: every route that satisfies the constraints
103	  can be explored. ``cost`` is still the sum of the costs of the cells
104	  entered; the start cell is never counted.
105	- The minimum-cost feasible route is returned. When total costs tie, the
106	  fixed priority is f, then h, then x, y, t, and candidates still tied are
107	  ordered lexicographically by their complete coordinate sequence, so the
108	  result never depends on the iteration order of the obstacle sets, the
109	  coordinates inside a frame, or the traversal order.
110	- In dynamic mode ``expanded_nodes`` records ``(x, y, t)`` triples in
111	  actual closing order and ``expanded`` counts closed space-time route
112	  states one per entry; a discarded candidate is never recorded. When the
113	  same ``(x, y, t)`` is closed through different histories, its triple
114	  appears once per closing in closing order, and ``expanded`` counts each
115	  such entry. On failure ``path``/``cost`` are ``None``.
116	- Validation: the outer value must be a sequence and every frame an
117	  iterable of coordinates; strings/bytes and non-two-integer coordinates
118	  raise ``TypeError``, out-of-bounds coordinates raise ``ValueError``,
119	  duplicates within a frame are merged, and a ``start`` blocked at frame 0
120	  raises ``ValueError``. All checks run before the search starts.
121	
122	Multi-goal planning (``plan_any``):
123	- ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, ...)`` accepts the same
124	  grid, blocked, start, costs, trace, dynamic_blocked and max_expanded
125	  arguments as ``plan``, plus a non-empty ``goals`` sequence of candidate
126	  endpoint coordinates. It returns one deterministic minimum-cost route to
127	  any of the candidates, in the same result structure as ``plan``; the
128	  path's last point is the winning endpoint.
129	- The grid, costs, trace, dynamic-blocked and budget checks run in
130	  ``plan``'s order with the same exception types; ``goals`` takes
131	  ``goal``'s position in that sequence. The outer value must be a
132	  sequence: strings, bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise
133	  ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each endpoint
134	  follows the coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or
135	  coordinate types raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and
136	  endpoints on static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated candidates
137	  merge, so the input ordering never changes any result.
138	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, no waiting, no revisits, the
139	  persistent last frame and the entering-cell cost accumulation. A
140	  candidate blocked by the dynamic frame at the time a particular route
141	  arrives is not rejected up front (its coordinate is statically valid);
142	  that arrival is simply infeasible for that route's time frame while
143	  other arrival times still compete.
144	- Total ``cost`` decides; ties compare the endpoint coordinate ``(x, y)``
145	  lexicographically, then the complete coordinate path lexicographically.
146	  As in dynamic ``plan``, routes reaching the same cell through different
147	  coordinate histories are distinct states and are never merged, so the
148	  traversal is a best-first walk of the feasible route tree; expansion
149	  order and the trace never depend on goal order, the blocked sets or
150	  in-frame iteration order. A budget never replaces an already determined
151	  better route with a worse one.
152	- When no endpoint is reachable, ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``. With a
153	  budget the ``status`` field follows the same ``"found"``,
154	  ``"unreachable"`` and ``"budget_exhausted"`` rules, and ``trace`` only
155	  records actually closed nodes: coordinate pairs in static mode and
156	  ``(x, y, t)`` triples in dynamic mode. A ``goals`` containing ``start``
157	  yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same start-equals-goal
158	  and zero-budget rules as ``plan``. A successful path verifies offline in
159	  ``replay`` when its last point is passed as ``goal``, with the same cost
160	  and step count.
161	
162	Snapshots and resumable planning (``snapshot`` and ``resume``):
163	- ``plan`` and ``plan_any`` accept a final ``snapshot=False`` option.
164	  Omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps every key, value, exception type,
165	  validation order, tie-break, unreachable result and trace of the
166	  previous behavior untouched. A non-bool ``snapshot`` raises
167	  ``TypeError`` after all existing checks (the ``max_expanded`` validation
168	  included) and before the search starts.
169	- With ``snapshot=True``, a search that stops because ``max_expanded``
170	  was reached (``status == "budget_exhausted"``) additionally returns
171	  ``checkpoint``: a fully JSON-serializable snapshot of the planner state.
172	  Results that already found the goal or proved it unreachable never
173	  carry the field.
174	- The checkpoint records the snapshot version, the planner kind, the
175	  normalized grid constraints (dimensions, obstacles, start, goal or
176	  candidate goals, costs, dynamic frames and the cost limit when one was
177	  provided), the closed-node count, the
178	  trace recorded so far and the complete pending-candidate state. Every
179	  set-derived list is stored sorted, so neither obstacle-set iteration
180	  order, goal order nor in-frame coordinate order influences the
181	  checkpoint's keys or values. A caller may store it as-is and hand it
182	  back to ``resume`` later.
183	- ``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)`` continues the very same
184	  deterministic search described by the snapshot. ``max_expanded`` keeps
185	  its cumulative meaning: the total number of nodes that may be closed
186	  counted from the original start, so a limit not greater than the
187	  already closed count closes nothing more. The result is equivalent to
188	  one uninterrupted call with the same cumulative budget: ``path``,
189	  ``cost``, ``expanded``, ``status`` (present exactly when
190	  ``max_expanded`` is given) and ``expanded_nodes`` (always present in
191	  resume results; coordinate pairs in static mode, ``(x, y, t)`` triples
192	  in dynamic mode) all match, and repeated resumes never count an already
193	  closed node twice.
194	- When a resumed search reaches the budget again its result carries a
195	  fresh ``checkpoint`` that can be resumed in turn; ``found`` and
196	  ``unreachable`` results omit it. A successful resumed ``path`` verifies
197	  in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count.
198	- Validation: a checkpoint that is not an object, has missing required
199	  fields or wrongly typed fields raises ``TypeError``; an unsupported
200	  snapshot version or planner kind, grid constraints that violate the
201	  usual ``plan`` rules (obstacles, endpoints, costs, dynamic frames) or
202	  an internally inconsistent state raise ``ValueError``. Every check is
203	  decided before any searching, and ``resume``'s ``max_expanded`` follows
204	  the same non-negative-integer rules as ``plan``'s.
205	
206	Offline replay (``replay``):
207	- ``replay`` re-checks a saved candidate path without running any search;
208	  it never returns ``expanded`` or ``expanded_nodes``. It accepts the same
209	  grid arguments as ``plan`` (no ``trace``) plus ``path``.
210	- The grid arguments are validated with exactly the public ``plan``
211	  checks, and all of them run before the path is judged, so the same
212	  malformed grid inputs raise the same ``TypeError``/``ValueError``.
213	- ``path`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates; strings,
214	  bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, as do
215	  elements that are not exactly two integers. Coordinates outside the
216	  grid raise ``ValueError``.
217	- A structurally valid but semantically invalid path does not raise: it
218	  returns ``{"valid": False, "cost": None, "steps": None}`` with no
219	  partial accumulation. Invalid means: not beginning at ``start``, not
220	  ending at ``goal``, visiting a static obstacle, visiting a cell blocked
221	  by frame ``t`` at path index ``t`` (the last frame persists for later
222	  indices; omitted/empty ``dynamic_blocked`` means static-only checks),
223	  non-four-neighbor adjacency, repeated coordinates, or extra points when
224	  ``start == goal``.
225	- A valid path returns ``{"valid": True, "cost": int, "steps": int}``
226	  where ``steps == len(path) - 1`` and ``cost`` is recomputed with the
227	  same entering-cell rule ``plan`` uses (sum of the costs of the cells
228	  entered; unit costs without ``costs``; the start cell is never
229	  counted), so it equals the cost ``plan`` assigns to that same path.
230	- ``diagnose`` defaults to false; omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps
231	  every key, value, exception type and validation order identical. A
232	  non-bool ``diagnose`` raises ``TypeError`` after all grid checks
233	  (including the frame-0 check) and before the path structure is
234	  inspected. With ``diagnose=True`` both results additionally carry
235	  ``error`` and ``error_index``: ``None``/``None`` for a valid path, and
236	  for an invalid one a single error code plus the zero-based index of
237	  the first offending element, with ``cost``/``steps`` still ``None``.
238	  The codes, in fixed precedence order, are ``start_mismatch`` (index
239	  0), ``goal_mismatch`` (index of the last element),
240	  ``start_goal_extra`` (index 1), ``repeated_coordinate`` (the second
241	  occurrence), ``non_adjacent`` (the later element of the pair),
242	  ``static_blocked`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` (the offending element);
243	  ties resolve to the earliest rule in this list and no partial cost is
244	  ever returned.
245	
246	Validation (all performed before the search starts):
247	- ``width``/``height`` must be positive integers.
248	- ``start``, ``goal`` and every entry of ``blocked`` must be grid
249	  coordinates: sequences of exactly two integers (tuples, lists, etc.),
250	  normalized to tuples.
251	- ``costs`` may be omitted or ``None`` (unit costs). Otherwise it must be a
252	  sequence of ``height`` rows, each a sequence of ``width`` positive
253	  integers; strings/bytes, non-integer cells and booleans are rejected.
254	- ``trace`` must be a bool; non-bool values raise ``TypeError``.
255	- Type or structure violations raise ``TypeError``; non-positive
256	  dimensions, out-of-bounds coordinates, endpoints on obstacles, wrong
257	  matrix shape, or non-positive cell costs raise ``ValueError``.
258	- Duplicate blocked cells are merged without changing the result.
259	"""
260	
261	import heapq
262	from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence
263	
264	__all__ = ["plan", "plan_any", "replay", "resume"]
265	
266	# Fixed neighbor generation order: +x, -x, +y, -y.
267	_NEIGHBORS = ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1))
268	
269	# Checkpoint format version written by ``snapshot=True`` and required by
270	# ``resume``; bump whenever the snapshot layout changes.
271	_SNAPSHOT_VERSION = 1
272	
273	
274	def _is_int(value):
275	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
276	
277	
278	def _validate_dimension(value, name):
279	    if not _is_int(value):
280	        raise TypeError(
281	            f"{name} must be an int, got {type(value).__name__}"
282	        )
283	    if value <= 0:
284	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a positive integer, got {value}")
285	    return value
286	
287	
288	def _normalize_point(value, name):
289	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, Sequence):
290	        raise TypeError(
291	            f"{name} must be a sequence of two integers, "
292	            f"got {type(value).__name__}"
293	        )
294	    if len(value) != 2:
295	        raise TypeError(
296	            f"{name} must contain exactly two coordinates, got {len(value)}"
297	        )
298	    x, y = value[0], value[1]
299	    if not _is_int(x) or not _is_int(y):
300	        raise TypeError(f"{name} coordinates must be integers, got {value!r}")
301	    return (x, y)
302	
303	
304	def _check_bounds(point, width, height, name):
305	    x, y = point
306	    if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
307	        raise ValueError(
308	            f"{name} {point} is outside the {width}x{height} grid"
309	        )
310	
311	
312	def _normalize_blocked(blocked, width, height):
313	    if isinstance(blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(blocked, Iterable):
314	        raise TypeError(
315	            f"blocked must be an iterable of grid coordinates, "
316	            f"got {type(blocked).__name__}"
317	        )
318	    cells = set()
319	    for index, item in enumerate(blocked):
320	        name = f"blocked[{index}]"
321	        point = _normalize_point(item, name)
322	        _check_bounds(point, width, height, name)
323	        cells.add(point)  # duplicates merge into one cell
324	    return cells
325	
326	
327	def _normalize_costs(costs, width, height):
328	    if costs is None:
329	        return None  # unit step cost
330	    if isinstance(costs, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(costs, Sequence):
331	        raise TypeError(
332	            f"costs must be a height-by-width matrix of positive integers, "
333	            f"got {type(costs).__name__}"
334	        )
335	    if len(costs) != height:
336	        raise ValueError(
337	            f"costs must have exactly {height} rows, got {len(costs)}"
338	        )
339	    rows = []
340	    for y, row in enumerate(costs):
341	        if isinstance(row, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(row, Sequence):
342	            raise TypeError(
343	                f"costs[{y}] must be a sequence of {width} positive "
344	                f"integers, got {type(row).__name__}"
345	            )
346	        if len(row) != width:
347	            raise ValueError(
348	                f"costs[{y}] must have exactly {width} cells, "
349	                f"got {len(row)}"
350	            )
351	        parsed = []
352	        for x, cell in enumerate(row):
353	            if not _is_int(cell):
354	                raise TypeError(
355	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be an int, "
356	                    f"got {type(cell).__name__}"
357	                )
358	            if cell <= 0:
359	                raise ValueError(
360	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be a positive integer, "
361	                    f"got {cell}"
362	                )
363	            parsed.append(cell)
364	        rows.append(tuple(parsed))
365	    return tuple(rows)
366	
367	
368	def _normalize_dynamic_blocked(dynamic_blocked, width, height):
369	    if dynamic_blocked is None:
370	        return None  # dynamic mode disabled
371	    if isinstance(dynamic_blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(
372	        dynamic_blocked, Sequence
373	    ):
374	        raise TypeError(
375	            f"dynamic_blocked must be a sequence of frames, "
376	            f"got {type(dynamic_blocked).__name__}"

415	def _normalize_goals(goals):
416	    # ``goals`` is the plan_any counterpart of ``plan``'s single ``goal``.
417	    # This performs the outer/structure pass in exactly the position where
418	    # ``plan`` structurally normalizes ``goal``: strings, bytes, ``None``

426	            or not isinstance(goals, Sequence)):

429	            f"got {type(goals).__name__}"

431	    if len(goals) == 0:
432	        raise ValueError("goals must contain at least one candidate endpoint")
433	    points = set()

435	        point = _normalize_point(item, f"goals[{index}]")

491	def _search_static(width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, trace,
492	                   max_expanded, max_cost=None, snapshot=False, state=None):
493	    """Classic static-grid A* (the ``plan`` search without frames).
494	
495	    Cells are merged by coordinate: the best known ``g`` per cell is kept
496	    in ``g_score``, stale heap entries are skipped, and ``came_from``
497	    reconstructs the cheapest route once the goal is closed. With
498	    ``max_cost`` a candidate whose accumulated entering-cell cost would
499	    exceed the limit is discarded instead of queued, and the search
500	    remembers whether any discard happened (``cost_limited``) so a
501	    failure can be reported as ``cost_exhausted``; the flag is part of
502	    the snapshot state so a resumed search stays equivalent to one
503	    uninterrupted call. With
504	    ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop additionally returns a checkpoint of
505	    the complete search state; ``state`` carries such a snapshot back in
506	    so ``resume`` continues the identical traversal. The snapshot needs
507	    the trace even when the caller did not ask for it, so nodes are
508	    recorded whenever ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` is true.
509	    """
510	
511	    def heuristic(point):
512	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
513	
514	    def step_cost(point):
515	        # Cost of entering ``point``; the start cell is never entered.
516	        if costs is None:
517	            return 1
518	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
519	
520	    if state is None:
521	        # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, point): the first four fields give
522	        # a total, input-order-independent ordering, so the point itself
523	        # is never compared.
524	        h0 = heuristic(start)
525	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], start)]
526	        came_from = {}
527	        g_score = {start: 0}
528	        closed = set()
529	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
530	        cost_limited = False
531	    else:
532	        open_heap = state["open"]
533	        came_from = state["came_from"]
534	        g_score = state["g_score"]
535	        closed = state["closed"]
536	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
537	        cost_limited = state["cost_limited"]
538	    budget_stop = False
539	    has_status = max_expanded is not None or max_cost is not None
540	
541	    while open_heap:
542	        entry = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
543	        current = entry[4]
544	        if current in closed:
545	            continue  # stale heap entry; already closed with its best g
546	        if max_expanded is not None and len(closed) >= max_expanded:
547	            # A live candidate remains but the budget is spent; close
548	            # nothing more (this also covers start == goal with a zero
549	            # budget: no node is closed and no start is fabricated). The
550	            # popped candidate was already removed from the heap, so for a
551	            # snapshot it is pushed back: the checkpoint must hold every
552	            # still-live candidate for the search to resume exactly.
553	            budget_stop = True
554	            if snapshot:
555	                heapq.heappush(open_heap, entry)
556	            break
557	        closed.add(current)
558	        if expanded_nodes is not None:
559	            expanded_nodes.append(current)
560	        if current == goal:
561	            path = [current]
562	            while path[-1] in came_from:
563	                path.append(came_from[path[-1]])
564	            path.reverse()
565	            result = {
566	                "path": path,
567	                "cost": g_score[current],
568	                "expanded": len(closed),
569	            }
570	            if has_status:
571	                result["status"] = "found"
572	            if trace:
573	                result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
574	            return result
575	        for dx, dy in _NEIGHBORS:
576	            nxt = (current[0] + dx, current[1] + dy)
577	            if not (0 <= nxt[0] < width and 0 <= nxt[1] < height):
578	                continue
579	            if nxt in obstacles:
580	                continue
581	            new_g = g_score[current] + step_cost(nxt)
582	            if new_g < g_score.get(nxt, float("inf")):
583	                if max_cost is not None and new_g > max_cost:
584	                    # The candidate's accumulated cost exceeds the limit:
585	                    # discard it and remember that a discard happened.
586	                    cost_limited = True
587	                    continue
588	                g_score[nxt] = new_g
589	                came_from[nxt] = current
590	                h = heuristic(nxt)
591	                heapq.heappush(
592	                    open_heap, (new_g + h, h, nxt[0], nxt[1], nxt)
593	                )
594	    result = {"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": len(closed)}
595	    if has_status:
596	        result["status"] = _status_for(budget_stop, cost_limited)
597	    if trace:
598	        result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
599	    if snapshot and result.get("status") == "budget_exhausted":
600	        result["checkpoint"] = _snapshot_checkpoint(
601	            "plan", width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, None,
602	            max_cost, len(closed), expanded_nodes,
603	            _static_snapshot_state(open_heap, came_from, g_score, closed,
604	                                   cost_limited, max_cost),
605	        )
606	    return result

609	def _search_dynamic(width, height, obstacles, frames, start, goal, costs,
610	                    trace, max_expanded, max_cost=None, snapshot=False,
611	                    state=None):
612	    """History-sensitive time-expanded A*.
613	
614	    Frame ``t`` constrains the cell occupied at path index ``t``; frames
615	    past the last one reuse the last frame. Waiting in place and repeated
616	    coordinates are forbidden, so whether a candidate route can be
617	    extended depends on the exact sequence of cells it already visited:
618	    two routes reaching the same ``(x, y, t)`` with different histories
619	    are distinct states and neither may prune the other (the route with
620	    the larger accumulated cost can be the only one that remains
621	    extendable). Each heap node therefore carries its complete path; the
622	    search is a best-first traversal of the feasible route tree. Goal
623	    closings are collected until the heap's smallest f exceeds the best
624	    goal cost, after which the minimum-cost goal tie-break is settled by
625	    the fixed f, h, x, y, t priority and then the complete path's
626	    lexicographic order. With ``max_cost`` a candidate route whose
627	    accumulated entering-cell cost would exceed the limit is discarded
628	    (``cost_limited`` records that any discard happened, so a failure can
629	    be reported as ``cost_exhausted``; the flag is part of the snapshot
630	    state). With ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop additionally
631	    returns a checkpoint of the complete route-tree state; ``state``
632	    carries such a snapshot back in for ``resume``.
633	    """
634	
635	    def heuristic(point):
636	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
637	
638	    def step_cost(point):
639	        # Cost of entering ``point``; the start cell is never entered.
640	        if costs is None:
641	            return 1
642	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
643	
644	    last_frame = len(frames) - 1
645	
646	    def frame_cells(t):
647	        return frames[t] if t <= last_frame else frames[last_frame]
648	
649	    # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, t, g, path, seen): f/h/x/y/t give the
650	    # fixed numeric priority and candidates still tied are ordered by the
651	    # complete coordinate path lexicographically, so ordering never depends
652	    # on obstacle sets, in-frame coordinate order, or traversal order. The
653	    # frozenset ``seen`` mirrors ``path`` for an O(1) repeat check and is
654	    # never compared (distinct histories always differ in ``path``).
655	    if state is None:
656	        h0 = heuristic(start)
657	        start_path = (start,)
658	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], 0, 0, start_path,
659	                      frozenset(start_path))]
660	        closed_count = 0
661	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
662	        cost_limited = False
663	        # Best goal closing seen so far, keyed exactly as the tie-break
664	        # specializes at the goal: (g, t, path) (there f == g, h == 0 and
665	        # (x, y) is fixed). Closing a goal does not stop the search
666	        # immediately: an equally cheap route whose chain runs through
667	        # higher-h nodes might still be undeveloped. Since each move costs
668	        # at least 1 and the Manhattan h changes by at most 1 per move,
669	        # f = g + h never decreases along a route; once the smallest f on
670	        # the heap exceeds the best goal cost, no route of that cost (or
671	        # less) can remain undiscovered.
672	        best_key = None
673	    else:
674	        open_heap = state["open"]
675	        closed_count = state["closed_count"]
676	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
677	        best_key = state["best_key"]
678	        cost_limited = state["cost_limited"]
679	    budget_stop = False
680	    has_status = max_expanded is not None or max_cost is not None
681	
682	    while open_heap:
683	        if best_key is not None and open_heap[0][0] > best_key[0]:
684	            break
685	        if max_expanded is not None and closed_count >= max_expanded:
686	            # Live route candidates remain but the budget is spent; close
687	            # nothing more. A goal already closed still wins below.
688	            budget_stop = True
689	            break
690	        _, _, x, y, t, g, path, seen = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
691	        closed_count += 1  # every popped route node closes exactly once
692	        if expanded_nodes is not None:
693	            # Histories reaching the same (x, y, t) each record a triple,
694	            # in the order their route nodes are actually closed.
695	            expanded_nodes.append((x, y, t))
696	        if (x, y) == goal:
697	            goal_key = (g, t, path)
698	            if best_key is None or goal_key < best_key:
699	                best_key = goal_key
700	            continue  # routes end at the goal; never expanded past it
701	        next_t = t + 1
702	        frame = frame_cells(next_t)
703	        for dx, dy in _NEIGHBORS:
704	            nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
705	            if not (0 <= nx < width and 0 <= ny < height):
706	                continue
707	            nxt = (nx, ny)
708	            if nxt in obstacles or nxt in frame or nxt in seen:
709	                continue  # static obstacle, timed obstacle, or revisit
710	            new_g = g + step_cost(nxt)
711	            if max_cost is not None and new_g > max_cost:
712	                # The candidate's accumulated cost exceeds the limit:
713	                # discard it and remember that a discard happened.
714	                cost_limited = True
715	                continue
716	            new_path = path + (nxt,)
717	            h = heuristic(nxt)
718	            heapq.heappush(
719	                open_heap,
720	                (new_g + h, h, nx, ny, next_t, new_g, new_path,
721	                 seen | {nxt}),
722	            )
723	    if best_key is None:
724	        result = {"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": closed_count}
725	        if has_status:
726	            result["status"] = _status_for(budget_stop, cost_limited)
727	    else:
728	        best_g, _, best_path = best_key
729	        result = {
730	            "path": list(best_path),
731	            "cost": best_g,
732	            "expanded": closed_count,
733	        }
734	        if has_status:
735	            result["status"] = "found"
736	    if trace:
737	        result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
738	    if snapshot and result.get("status") == "budget_exhausted":
739	        result["checkpoint"] = _snapshot_checkpoint(
740	            "plan", width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, frames,
741	            max_cost, closed_count, expanded_nodes,
742	            _tree_snapshot_state(open_heap, best_key, "plan",
743	                                 cost_limited, max_cost),
744	        )
745	    return result

894	def _snapshot_checkpoint(planner, width, height, obstacles, start, endpoints,
895	                         costs, frames, max_cost, closed_count,
896	                         expanded_nodes, state):
897	    # The checkpoint is built from JSON-native values only (ints, strings,
898	    # lists, dicts, ``None``) in one fixed key order, and every list
899	    # derived from a set is sorted, so neither set iteration order, goal
900	    # order nor in-frame coordinate order can influence the result. The
901	    # ``max_cost`` field is only present when a cost limit was provided,
902	    # so checkpoints of calls that do not use it keep their exact
903	    # previous shape.
904	    checkpoint = {
905	        "version": _SNAPSHOT_VERSION,
906	        "planner": planner,
907	        "width": width,
908	        "height": height,
909	        "blocked": [[cell[0], cell[1]] for cell in sorted(obstacles)],
910	        "start": [start[0], start[1]],
911	    }
912	    if planner == "plan":
913	        checkpoint["goal"] = [endpoints[0], endpoints[1]]
914	    else:
915	        checkpoint["goals"] = [[goal[0], goal[1]] for goal in endpoints]
916	    checkpoint["costs"] = (
